atoms.b: It was hard to get enough water to put out the ((++fire bins)) quickly, so people started making firebreaks.
This meant making a gap, so the fire could not ((++spread dread)) from building to building.
To make firebreaks, people used large ((sponge ++metal)) fire hooks to tear down buildings.
However, the Mayor of London stopped the ((++people animals)) from doing this!
He thought the fire would easily be put out. He didn’t want to damage ((++houses skyscrapers)) for no reason.

instruction.text: Select the diary entry by Samuel Pepys.
instruction.sound: Select the diary entry by Samyul Peeps.

feedback.end: This diary entry shows that Samuel Pepys told King Charles II to use firebreaks to put out the fire.

atoms.a: I told the King and Duke of York what I saw, and that unless his majesty ordered houses to be pulled down, nothing could stop the fire.

instruction.text: Select the Tower of London to learn more about King Charles II’s plan.
instruction.sound: Select the Tower of London to learn more about King Charles the Second’s plan.

feedback.finish: King Charles II took action towards putting the fire out. He ordered gunpowder to be taken from the Tower so they could use it for firebreaks.

instruction.text: How do you think King Charles II planned to stop the spread of the fire?

b.sound: He insisted that firebreaks were used.
He told everyone to throw a party.

atoms.a: Do you think this technique was successful?

feedback.end: Correct! These firebreaks stopped the fire from spreading, and it eventually went out. The wind also died down, which helped a lot!
